unresolved: Numerical inverse inequality constant C_tau for degree2-4 local spaces is not specified in the numerical subsection.
Exact triangle connectivity and quadrature are not given.
Figure3 abscissas are approximately Table1 H values divided by sqrt(2); the conversion is not explained.
Roundoff-level mass defects cannot be used as portable digit-by-digit acceptance targets.
norm_discrepancies: Equation55 defines the full pseudostress -nu*grad(u)+p*I. Figure3 L2 pseudostress ordinates closely track the velocity gradient error. Full-stress values are incompatible with these ordinates for our reconstructed fields, as verified by the measured pressure, gradient and divergence norms; original coefficient arrays are unavailable, so this does not identify a bug in the article.

Equation8 defines a norm on conforming H(div;Omega) weighting divergence by domain diameter squared. The numerical section names a broken H(div;T_H) norm without repeating its weight. Figure3 is matched by divergence weight1; both conventions are reported without asserting a formal contradiction.

Figure4 velocity and pressure curves agree within1percent at the first five levels; stress curves remain discrepant. Orthogonal projection of f onto P2 or a larger polynomial space can only reduce the divergence residual and cannot explain the larger published H(div) ordinate.

comparison_evidence.crisscross_p2_p2_trace0: 20 values across velocity L2, velocity H1 seminorm, pressure L2 and standard broken pseudostress H(div), n4 through64, differ by at most0.14 percent.
comparison_evidence.crisscross_p3_p3_trace1: 15 velocity and pressure values, n4,8,16,32,64, differ by at most0.70 percent.
comparison_evidence.constant_definition: Largest admissible scalar constant from the generalized Laplacian/gradient eigenproblem, quotienting constant functions; no curve-fitting.
